scope: M4 design exploration: (1) intensity band easy/steady/hard in the plan UI + a race-pace session treatment + an honest intensity ramp legend; (2) onboarding anchored on pace with a live derived-pace preview. Design only — no app code changed.

core_device.name: IntensityLadder
core_device.shape: A fixed 3-slot ladder mark: three discrete cells with a hairline gap, filled bottom/left-up to the session's band. easy = 1 lit (▓··), steady = 2 lit (▓▓·), hard = 3 lit (▓▓▓). No fourth state.
core_device.why_one_glyph: One mark, rendered at three sizes, is what lets intensity appear on the card, the week strip and the week list WITHOUT a new row, a new colour, or a new card shape. The user learns the glyph once (in the legend and in onboarding) and reads it everywhere.
core_device.colour_rule: Lit cells = --ink (a prescription is ink, not a measurement). Unlit cells = --hairline-strong outline at 3:1. Band is encoded by COUNT, never by hue, so it survives greyscale and colour-blind simulation. --signal (amber) is NOT used for the band: amber stays reserved for measurement/now (goal-pace marker, today, current phase, needle).
core_device.derivation: band = f(archetype, targetRpe), pure and testable in packages/shared. Rule: if prescription.targetRpe exists use its upper bound (<=5 easy, 6-7 steady, >=8 hard); else fall back to archetype: {easy,recovery,long,mobility,cross-train}->easy, {tempo,threshold,strides,machine-circuit,full-body-strength}->steady, {interval,hills,fartlek,race}->hard. No new stored field; computed at the edge like units.
core_device.data_source: SessionArchetype + SessionPrescription.targetRpe (packages/shared/src/types.ts); engine PURPOSE/TITLE (apps/api + plan/engine.ts). Honest: the band is a summary of data the engine already emits, not a new invented metric.

wires.screen: 4. Intensity key + progression cue — how intensity ramps across phases
wires.ascii:
INTENSITY ▾
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▓··  EASY     easy · recovery · long · strength           │
│                conversational; most of your running       │
│ ▓▓·  STEADY   tempo · threshold · strides                 │
│                'comfortably hard' — short sentences       │
│ ▓▓▓  HARD     intervals · hills · race                    │
│                controlled reps; form holds                │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

WHERE THE PLAN IS GOING            (derived from your phase rules)
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            BASE      BUILD      PEAK      TAPER          │
│ ceiling     ▓·        ▓▓        ▓▓▓        ▓▓            │
│           (steady)  (steady+)  (hard)   (hold effort)     │
│ vol   ▬▬▬   ▬▬▬▬▬▬    ▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬   ▬▬▬▬     ▬▬▬            │
│  W5 ───▲─────────                                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Two honest, discrete encodings — no fake smooth curve:
   'ceiling' = the highest intensity band the phase actually schedules (1 / 2 / 3 / 2);
   'vol' = a hairline rule whose LENGTH is the phase's peak weekly volume from the
   engine's volume curve (rises through build/peak, drops in taper). The only amber is
   the '▲ you are here' notch on the current phase/week.

notes.intent: Answer 'why are some weeks hard and some calm' with two real, discrete facts, not a fabricated performance chart. It teaches the plan's architecture at the moment the user is looking at the strip and the list.

'you are here' notch = --signal (mark only) + a text label 'W5 · base'
no red/amber/green intensity colour-coding

copy.stale_note: Times older than ~6 months drift — add a fresher one when you can.
copy.fallback: No race to hand? We start you at a comfortable easy band and keep the build conservative. Your first few logged runs recalibrate every pace above.
copy.fallback_provisional: Threshold and interval unlock after your first logged runs. Goal pace isn't set yet.
copy.guardrail_fast: That time is very fast for a starting plan — we'll cap the weekly build and recalibrate after your first runs.
copy.guardrail_slow: All good — everyone starts somewhere. We'll begin easy and the paces will tighten as you get fitter.
copy.recalibrated_later: Your paces were recalibrated from your last 3 logged runs.

fallback.trigger: The user picks 'NO RECENT RACE', or the race path is left empty and they continue.
fallback.derivation: Use Baseline.experience + Baseline.weeklyKm, exactly the two fields the engine's baseWeeklyKm already consumes. Produce a conservative easy band (slower end first) and a provisional VDOT ceiling; do not print threshold/interval/goal as if measured.
fallback.recalibration: After the first 1-3 logged runs, recompute paces from actual average pace at a known RPE and surface 'Your paces were recalibrated from your last 3 logged runs' on the plan. This is the safety that makes a conservative fallback honest.
fallback.escape_hatch: 'I'LL ADD A RACE TIME LATER' keeps a re-entry point into this same step from plan settings; paces stay provisional until then.

motion.name: ladder-fill-once
motion.trigger: First paint of a card, strip cell, or preview row, once per session id / once per onboarding mount
motion.spec: lit cells reveal left->right (card/list) or bottom->top (strip) with 14ms stagger; unlit outlines present from the start; band meaning does not depend on the animation
motion.reduced_motion: No stagger, no transform: final state, opacity 120ms

motion.name: preview-update
motion.spec: pace numerals swap instantly; row set cross-fades 120ms; ladder cells step 90ms; live region speaks once after 400ms
motion.reduced_motion: Instant; only the live-region announcement remains

motion.name: phase-notch-draw
motion.spec: the amber 'you are here' notch draws once; ceiling ladders and volume rules are static

motion.name: goal-pace-marker
motion.spec: ◎ fades in with the inherited needle-settle; no pulse, no flash, no rotation

motion.name: press-step / sheet-rise / why-expand
motion.spec: 90ms background step; 220ms sheet rise; 180ms grid-rows expand
motion.reduced_motion: Instant per the global reduce block in app.css

motion.name: ANTI-RULE: numerals and paces never animate
motion.spec: Every derived pace, VDOT, distance and volume swaps instantly. No count-up, no odometer, no scrolling digits. Tabular figures exist so values do not reflow; animating them is unreadable mid-effort and dishonest about precision.

a11y.requirement: The band is the COUNT of lit ladder cells plus a real word: card band line ('steady'), strip/list accessible names ('hard'), and the key's definition text. Greyscale and colour-blind simulation must preserve the band. Lit=--ink (15.9:1), unlit outline=--hairline-strong (3:1) — both above their bars.

--signal is mark-only: the goal-pace ◎, the today ring/underline, the current-phase notch, the modality edge. Band never uses amber. Amber TEXT (provenance '›', derivation caret, logged ✓) uses --signal-ink: 5.3:1 light, 10.7:1 dark. --signal as text (#E8A33D on #F4F5F2 = 1.97:1) remains forbidden.

Card heading: 'Tempo run, steady, 6 kilometres'. Strip cell: 'Thursday 21 November, intervals, hard, not logged'. List row: 'Thursday, intervals, hard, 4 kilometres, not logged'. Ladder glyphs are aria-hidden so they never double-speak.

Persistent labels above fields (no placeholder-as-label); time input inputmode=numeric, pace inputmode=decimal; unit inside the accessible name; >=16px input text to stop iOS zoom; errors inline with aria-live=polite + aria-invalid, never colour-only.

The pace preview is a <dl>; derived paces are announced once through one polite live region after a 400ms debounce, in complete sentences, never per keystroke and never assertively. VDOT is announced with its unit meaning ('VDOT 47'), not as a bare number.

Locked/provisional rows say so in TEXT ('threshold, provisional — unlocks after your first logged runs'), never by faded colour alone. Goal pace reads 'not set yet' when it is not set. No fabricated numbers are rendered with the same weight as real ones.
>=44px everywhere. The ladder marks add no tap target — they live inside existing 44px+ rows, cells, and wells. Mode radios, day cells, segments and steppers are all >=44px.

2px --signal-ink outline, 2px paper offset on :focus-visible only, visible on paper, sunken, inside the amber band and inside the sticky preview. Focus never moves on live update; the typed field keeps focus.

prefers-reduced-motion kills every stagger, draw, notch and cross-fade; only 90-120ms opacity/colour steps remain. app.css already zeroes durations globally; components must still land on the correct FINAL state (lit ladder, drawn notch) rather than an empty one.
No fixed heights on text; at 200% zoom the preview rows and the PhaseRail reflow to stacked rows, and the band degrades to its word in every case. The accessible name is always the source of truth.

self_critique.ascii_legend: ▓ = lit ladder cell (ink) · = unlit cell / rest. ▓·· easy, ▓▓· steady, ▓▓▓ hard. ◎ = goal-pace marker (amber, mark only). ▾/▸ = disclosure/caret (signal-ink). ▬ = hairline-strong volume rule. ▲ = current-week notch (amber). ✓ = logged. ● = planned. (22) = today ring.

templated_defaults_avoided.how: No serif, no cream (paper is cool green-grey #F4F5F2), no terracotta. All display/heading type is Space Grotesk; warmth is the single amber, used as a mark (◎, notch) not a surface.
Dark is #101318 (blue-black), not #0A0A0A; the accent is amber, never acid; no glow, no gradient mesh, no neon intensity colours. Intensity is encoded by COUNT, not by a traffic-light hue.

templated_defaults_avoided.default: Broadsheet hairlines only — thin rules doing all the work
templated_defaults_avoided.how: Hairlines are the quiet layer; the data layer is the ladder (discrete filled cells), the structure rows, the volume rule, and --hairline-strong specifically because hairline-only would make the instrument parts invisible.

other_defaults_avoided: No red/yellow/green intensity colour-coding — the single most templated way to do 'easy/steady/hard', and the least accessible. Banned here: band is count + word.
No fake 'readiness' line, no smooth intensity curve, no gradient gauge. The progression cue draws only what the engine can derive (phase ceilings + relative volume).
No emoji intensity badges (🔥💪😤) and no icon-per-row; the only glyphs are the ladder, ◎, ✓, ▾.
No progress ring for 'intensity' and no streak flame.
No new row bolted onto the session card — the band rides the existing eyebrow row and band line, proving the card shape is a system, not a layout to be broken.
No amber CTA. The build button stays ink-fill/paper-label.

risks.risk: The horizontal 3-cell ladder could be misread as a progress bar (sessions done).
risks.mitigation: The ladder always sits adjacent to the WORD 'easy/steady/hard', never alone; it is 3 discrete gapped cells (▓·· ) so it can't be read as a continuous fill; completion is a different mark (✓). The legend pairs the glyph with its word the first time.

risks.risk: Amber creeps into the band (it is tempting to tint hard days amber).
risks.mitigation: Band is ink-only by rule; amber is defined as measurement/now. If a hard day is amber, that is a bug. The goal-pace ◎ is the one amber intensity-adjacent mark, and it means 'race pace', not 'hard'.

risks.risk: The fallback (no race) preview looks empty or fake.
risks.mitigation: It shows a real conservative easy band (from experience + volume via the engine's own baseWeeklyKm) and marks the rest provisional/unlockable, with a recalibration promise. Nothing pretends to be measured.

risks.risk: Goal pace is shown for a profile that has no race (whole-fitness).
risks.mitigation: Harmony rule: no goal/race pace if it can't be derived; race-pace sessions don't exist for whole-fitness; the preview row reads 'not set yet'.

risks.risk: Mono + ladders everywhere makes the app read as a spreadsheet of marks.
risks.mitigation: Marks are restricted to (a) the band ladder, (b) the single amber measurement mark per surface. Prose stays Plex Sans; mono stays numerals + short caps.

rejected.option: Colour-code intensity (e.g. blue/green/red or a graded amber).
rejected.reason: Fails AA in greyscale and colour-blindness, breaks the 'amber is a mark, not a scale' rule, and re-introduces the traffic-light default the world is trying to avoid.

rejected.option: A fourth band or five-zone display.
rejected.reason: More bands than the engine's effort data cleanly supports; risks the user having to learn a vocabulary mid-run. Three maps to RPE/Z bands that already exist.

rejected.option: A smooth 'intensity over the plan' line chart.
rejected.reason: 'No fake charts.' A fitted line would imply continuous data we don't have; discrete phase ceilings + a volume rule are honest and cheaper.

rejected.option: Make the card's modality edge encode intensity.
rejected.reason: The edge already encodes modality (signal=run, steel=strength); overloading it would make two facts fight in one 1.5px channel and break the established card.
One anchor is enough for the engine and lowers the form burden; four blank fields read as a test.

open_questions: Should the strip show a double day as the day's peak band, or split the cell into two thin ladders? I chose peak + accessible detail to keep the 7-column axis.
Does 'current easy pace' invert cleanly to a VDOT without a race, or should it stay a display-only band and defer threshold/interval until a race time exists?
Where exactly does the PhaseRail live — week header, plan overview, or a settings 'about this plan' screen — without competing with the session card?
Recalibration from logged runs: what RPE threshold counts as 'a known effort' before we trust the derived paces?
